name: Bagalkot
monumentDescription: Four 6th–8th century rock-cut sandstone sanctuaries excavated into red cliffs overlooking Agastya Lake, featuring Cave 3's dated 578 CE inscription.
culturalSignificance: Crucible of Early Chalukyan temple architecture bridging Nagara and Dravida styles alongside nearby Pattadakal (UNESCO Ref. 239) and Aihole.
monumentAttribution: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & UNESCO World Heritage Centre
description: Home to the Malaprabha River basin sites of Badami, Aihole, and Pattadakal, representing the formative crucible of Early Chalukyan temple architecture.
history: Badami (ancient Vatapi) served as the royal capital of the Early Chalukyas from the 6th to 8th centuries CE. Cave 3 at Badami contains an inscribed record dated to 578 CE under ruler Mangalesha.
heritageSites: Group of Monuments at Pattadakal (UNESCO Ref. 239, 1987)

name: Ballari
geoBoundaryNote: In the 2021 geoBoundaries LGD boundary layer, this polygon encompasses both Ballari and Vijayanagara (carved out in November 2021).
monumentDescription: Two-tiered granite hill fortress rising atop Bellary Gudda, constructed under Hanumappa Nayaka during the Vijayanagara era and reinforced in the 18th century.
culturalSignificance: Marks the eastern Deccan frontier linking Vijayanagara-period hill defense architecture with later Mysore Sultanate masonry.
monumentAttribution: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) Protected Monument
description: Mineral-rich Deccan plateau district historically linked with the Vijayanagara imperial frontier and Bellary Fort.
history: Ballari district bordered the Vijayanagara heartland until November 17, 2021, when Vijayanagara district (headquartered at Hospet) was carved out as Karnataka's 31st district.

sources.title: Karnataka District Gazetteer & Vijayanagara District Formation (2021)

name: Belagavi
monumentDescription: 13th-century stone fortress initiated by the Ratta dynasty of Saundatti, enclosing the carved Chalukyan-style Kamala Basadi Jain shrine and Adil Shahi bastions.
culturalSignificance: Illustrates layered Deccan heritage where Ratta Jain temple architecture coexists with Safa Masjid and colonial-era cantonment history.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage
description: Borderland northern Karnataka district anchored by the Ratta-era Belagavi Fort and Sahyadri hill passes; full festival and craft monographs are currently under compilation.
history: Historically known as Venugrama, Belagavi flourished under the Ratta rulers before passing through Vijayanagara, Adil Shahi, Maratha, and British administrations.

name: Bengaluru Rural
monumentDescription: Oval granite bastion fortress built around 1501 CE by Malla Byregowda of the Avati chieftains and later rebuilt in dressed stone under Hyder Ali.
culturalSignificance: Preserves 16th-century mud-to-granite civic fortification techniques and houses centuries-old Venugopalaswamy and Siddheshwara temples.
description: Highland agricultural district encircling the capital, anchored by Devanahalli Fort and Avati Nadaprabhu heritage; full district cultural records are under review.
history: Devanahalli emerged under Avati chieftain Malla Byregowda in 1501 CE before becoming an important Mysore garrison in the 18th century.

name: Bengaluru Urban
monumentDescription: Two-storey Indo-Islamic pavilion completed in 1791 CE using carved teak pillars, cusped arches, and floral frescoes adjacent to Bangalore Fort.
culturalSignificance: Rare surviving 18th-century timber-framed court residence of the Mysore Sultanate beside the 1537 CE Kempegowda urban core.
description: Capital district of Karnataka blending Kempegowda-era urban tanks and pete markets with 18th-century court architecture and civic botanical gardens.
history: Founded in 1537 CE by Kempe Gowda I with fortified enclosures and interconnected temple tanks; later served as an administrative and botanical hub in southern India.

name: Bidar
monumentDescription: 15th-century Bahmani Sultanate citadel built along the edge of a red laterite plateau, featuring triple moats, glazed Persian tilework, and karez water channels.
culturalSignificance: Center of Deccan Indo-Persian architecture, historic karez subterranean aqueducts, and GI-certified Bidriware silver-inlay metalcraft (GI No. 21).
monumentAttribution: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) & World Monuments Fund
description: Northernmost plateau district famed for Bahmani fort architecture, karez subterranean water engineering, and GI-certified Bidriware silver-inlay metalcraft.
history: Served as the capital of the Bahmani Sultanate from the 15th century CE and later the Barid Shahi kingdom, nurturing Persian-Deccan architecture and metallurgy.
traditions: Tarkashi Silver Inlay & Bidar Fort Soil Oxidation

name: Chamarajanagar
monumentDescription: Cliff-top Dravidian shrine perched at 1,550 meters elevation where the Western and Eastern Ghats converge, revered across Soliga and regional communities.
culturalSignificance: Embodies biocultural coexistence within the BRT forested landscape alongside Male Mahadeshwara Hills and Chamarajeshwara Temple.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Endowments & Forest Heritage Documentation
description: Southernmost ecological corridor linking the Nilgiris and Eastern Ghats; detailed district festival and craft archives are currently being verified.
history: Named after Chamaraja Wadiyar IX, the region preserves Soliga forest traditions and hill sanctuaries supported by regional dynasties.

name: Chikkaballapura
monumentLocation: Nandi Village, Foothills of Nandi Hills
monumentDescription: Ancient granite temple complex founded under Bana and Nolamba patronage in the 9th century CE and expanded by Chola, Hoysala, and Vijayanagara dynasties.
culturalSignificance: Remarkable palimpsest of five southern Indian dynasties visible in its carved kalyani stepped tank, lattice screens, and pillared mandapas.
description: Granite hill district at the source of the Arkavathi and Palar rivers; full intangible heritage records are currently under compilation.
history: Situated beneath Nandi Durga hill fort, the Nandi temple complex records continuous inscriptions spanning Bana, Nolamba, Chola, and Vijayanagara rule.

name: Chikkamagaluru
monumentDescription: 1196 CE Hoysala soapstone shrine commissioned by general Amriteshwara Dandanayaka, famed for its scalloped mantapa ceilings and epic narrative friezes.
culturalSignificance: Showcases mature Hoysala chloritic schist artistry nestled in the Malnad foothills alongside Sringeri and Belavadi.
description: Western Ghats coffee and temple highland spanning Mullayanagiri, Sringeri, and Amruthapura; full district cultural dossiers are in preparation.
history: Known as the cradle of Hoysala origins near Sosevur (Angadi) and home to the 8th-century Sringeri Sharada Peetham.

name: Chitradurga
monumentDescription: Seven-ringed granite boulder fortress engineered by the Madakari Nayaka dynasty between the 14th and 18th centuries with interconnected rainwater reservoirs.
culturalSignificance: Masterpiece of Deccan military hydrology and hero-lore remembering Obavva and the Chitradurga Nayakas.
description: Central Deccan fort-town dominated by the seven concentric stone ramparts of Chitradurga Fort; detailed folklore records are currently being archived.
history: Rose to prominence under the Nayakas of Chitradurga, who transformed natural granite outcrops into an interconnected water-harvesting citadel.

name: Dakshina Kannada
monumentDescription: 10th–11th century coastal shrine housing rare dated 968 CE Chola-period bronze Lokeshwara statues, laterite tiered roofs, and stepped natural spring tanks.
culturalSignificance: Reflects coastal Tuluva syncretic heritage linking Natha traditions, monsoon laterite architecture, Tenkuthittu Yakshagana, and Kambala.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Department of Archaeology & KSTDC
description: Coastal Tuluva region renowned for Tenkuthittu Yakshagana theatre, seasonal Kambala buffalo-race traditions, and coastal temple architecture.
history: Situated between the Arabian Sea and Western Ghats, Dakshina Kannada developed distinctive Tulu-Kannada cultural and maritime trading traditions.

name: Davanagere
monumentDescription: Monumental 16th-century stepped stone water tank flanked by an octagonal Vasant Mantapa pavilion built by local Nayaka chieftain Kenga Hanumappa.
culturalSignificance: Celebrated example of post-Vijayanagara hydraulic and Indo-Islamic pavilion synthesis alongside Harihareshwara Temple.
description: Central plains district featuring the Santhebennur Pushkarani and Hoysala-era Harihareshwara Temple; full archival entries are being verified.
history: Historically linked with the Basavapatna Nayakas and medieval Tungabhadra riverine trade corridors.

name: Dharwad
monumentDescription: 12th-century Kalyana Chalukyan cruciform sandstone temple distinguished by four ornate cardinal doorways and pierced stone latticework.
culturalSignificance: Anchors Dharwad's medieval Chalukyan sculptural heritage alongside its modern renown for Hindustani music gharanas and GI-tagged Dharwad Peda.
description: Cultural and literary capital of northern Karnataka, celebrated for Hindustani classical music traditions and GI-certified Dharwad Peda.
history: Nurtured major Hindustani classical vocalists and literary figures across modern Karnataka, while the Thakur family introduced Dharwad Peda over 175 years ago.

sources.title: Geographical Indications Registry — Application No. 80 (Dharwad Pedha)

name: Gadag
monumentDescription: 11th-century Kalyana Chalukya soapstone masterwork celebrated for deeply undercut stone toranas, twin shrines, and over 100 ancient stepped wells.
culturalSignificance: Bridge between Early Chalukyan stone carving and ornate Hoysala sculpture, accompanied by the Trikuteshwara Temple in Gadag.
description: Home to the Kalyana Chalukya temple clusters of Lakkundi, Dambal, and Gadag; full festival and craft documentation is in progress.
history: Lakkundi (ancient Lokkigundi) served as a prominent royal mint and architectural center of the Kalyana Chalukyas in the 10th–12th centuries CE.

name: Hassan
monumentDescription: 12th-century UNESCO-inscribed Hoysala chloritic schist sanctuary built in 1117 CE on a stellate plinth with lathe-turned pillars and signed sculptures.
culturalSignificance: Flagship of the Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas (UNESCO Ref. 1670) alongside Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu and Shravanabelagola.
description: Heartland of the Hoysala Empire, housing the UNESCO-inscribed chloritic schist sanctuaries of Belur and Halebidu.
history: Initiated in the 12th century CE under King Vishnuvardhana at Belur and Dorasamudra (Halebidu), Hoysala temple workshops created signed soapstone sculptures on stellate plinths.

name: Haveri
monumentDescription: 11th-century Kalyana Chalukyan sandstone temple marked by a distinctive pyramidal stepped shikhara towering along the Tungabhadra-Varada river confluence.
culturalSignificance: Celebrated for Chalukyan stepped-tower geometry and nearby Siddhesvara Temple and Kaginele literary heritage.
description: Tungabhadra riverine district rich in Chalukyan temples at Galaganatha, Haveri, and Bankapura; detailed cultural entries are in progress.
history: Flourished along ancient river crossings under the Kalyana Chalukyas and later gave rise to Kanakadasa's bhakti poetry at Kaginele.

name: Kalaburagi
monumentDescription: 14th-century Bahmani stone fortress housing 15 watchtowers, a rare fully roofed 63-dome Jama Masjid (1367 CE), and the Bara Gazi cannon.
culturalSignificance: First capital of the Bahmani Sultanate (1347–1424 CE), showcasing early Deccan arched vaulting and Haft Gumbaz tombs.
description: Historic Kalyana Karnataka center preserving Bahmani stone citadels, Sannati-adjacent Buddhist links, and Sufi heritage; full archive records pending.
history: Served as the founding Bahmani capital from 1347 CE before the court relocated north to Bidar.

name: Kodagu
monumentDescription: 17th-century hilltop citadel built in mud by Muddu Raja and rebuilt in granite under Tipu Sultan and Lingarajendra Wadiyar II.
culturalSignificance: Anchors Kodagu's highland history alongside community-guarded Devarakadu sacred forest groves and Kodava harvest traditions.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Department of Archaeology & Forest Department
description: Highland Western Ghats district known for community-guarded Devarakadu sacred forest groves, Kodava cultural customs, and headwater conservation.
history: Home to ancestral Kodava communities and hundreds of sacred Devarakadu forest patches protected through village taboos and Forest Department co-management.
cuisine: Kodava Akki Otti & Bamboo Shoot Preparations

name: Kolar
monumentDescription: Granite Vijayanagara-period Someshwara complex famed for its ornate kalyana mandapa and sculpted dravidian gopura beside 11th-century Chola inscriptions.
culturalSignificance: Preserves rare early Western Ganga and Chola-period stone reliefs alongside Antargange and Kurudumale.
description: Ancient Eastern Maidan district known as Kuvalalapura under the Western Gangas; full cultural dossiers are currently under compilation.
history: Served as an early capital of the Western Ganga dynasty before Chola and Vijayanagara temple expansions.

name: Koppal
monumentDescription: 1112 CE Kalyana Chalukyan soapstone sanctuary lauded in contemporary epigraphs as 'Devalaya Chakravarti' (Emperor among Temples).
culturalSignificance: Monumental zenith of 12th-century Chalukyan carved ceilings and 68-pillar open mandapa near Ashokan rock edicts at Koppal.
description: Tungabhadra-Anegundi heartland preserving Ashokan edicts, Koppal Fort, and the 1112 CE Mahadeva Temple at Itagi; full records in preparation.
history: Celebrated across Mauryan, Rashtrakuta, Kalyana Chalukya, and early Vijayanagara (Anegundi) history.

sources.title: Mahadeva Temple at Itagi Monument Record

name: Mandya
monumentDescription: 1784 CE teakwood garden palace adorned with vivid battle and court murals within the historic Kaveri island citadel of Srirangapatna.
culturalSignificance: Unites 9th-century Ranganathaswamy temple heritage with 18th-century Mysore court murals and river island fortifications.
description: Fertile Kaveri basin district anchored by the historic island capital of Srirangapatna and Hoysala temples at Kikkeri and Hosaholalu.
history: Srirangapatna served as provincial seat under Vijayanagara and royal capital of Mysuru prior to 1799 CE.

name: Mysuru
monumentDescription: Indo-Saracenic royal residence rebuilt between 1897 and 1912 CE under the Wadiyar dynasty, blending Rajput domes, stained glass, and carved rosewood halls.
culturalSignificance: Focal stage for Karnataka's Nada Habba Mysuru Dasara, Mysore Traditional Paintings (GI No. 32), and KSIC Mysore Silk (GI No. 22).
monumentAttribution: Mysore Palace Board & Karnataka State Tourism (KSTDC)
description: Cultural capital of southern Karnataka, anchored by Amba Vilas Palace, Nada Habba Mysuru Dasara, Mysore Traditional Paintings, and KSIC Mysore Silk.
history: Under the Wadiyar dynasty, Mysuru developed a renowned synthesis of Indo-Saracenic architecture, classical music, gold-gilded gesso painting, and pure mulberry silk weaving.

sources.title: Geographical Indications Registry — GI App. Nos. 22 & 32

name: Raichur
monumentDescription: 1294 CE Kakatiya-built hill fortress erected by Gore Gangaya Reddivaru, notable for its cyclopean dry-stone ramparts and a monumental 12-meter inscribed monolith.
culturalSignificance: Key strategic monument of the Krishna–Tungabhadra Raichur Doab alongside Maski's Ashokan inscription.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage
description: Historic Krishna–Tungabhadra Doab district famous for Raichur Fort and the Maski Ashokan edict; detailed cultural records are currently in compilation.
history: The Maski edict here famously recorded Emperor Ashoka's personal name ('Devanampriya Ashoka'), while Raichur Fort changed hands between Kakatiyas, Bahmanis, and Vijayanagara.

name: Ramanagara
monumentDescription: Granite hill sanctuary crowned by medieval stone mandapas and steps rising above the historic Channapatna artisan corridor.
culturalSignificance: Links monumental granite hill-shrines with Channapatna ('Gombegala Ooru'), internationally protected under GI No. 23 for botanical lac-finished wooden toys.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Tourism (KSTDC) & IP India GI Registry
description: Home to Channapatna ('Gombegala Ooru'), internationally recognized for botanical lac-finished wooden toys protected under Geographical Indication status.
history: Historical craft patronage dates back over two centuries to Tipu Sultan, who invited Persian artisans to train local lathe-turners working with Wrightia tinctoria timber.
arts: Channapatna Wooden Toys & Dolls (GI App. No. 23, 2006)

sources.title: Geographical Indications Registry — Application No. 23 (Channapatna Toys & Dolls)

name: Shivamogga
monumentDescription: 16th-century granite sanctuary built by the Keladi Nayakas, uniting Vijayanagara mandapas with coastal sloping eaves and a Nandi pavilion.
culturalSignificance: Testament to the Keladi Nayaka kingdom alongside Keladi Rameshwara Temple, Kavaledurga Fort, and Balligavi.
description: Malnad gateway housing the Keladi Nayaka monuments of Ikkeri and Kavaledurga alongside Balligavi and Kudali; full archival entries pending.
history: Ruled successively by Kadambas, Chalukyas, Hoysalas, and the Keladi Nayakas whose 16th-century capital stood at Ikkeri and Bidanur.

name: Tumakuru
monumentDescription: 17th-century hilltop fortification rising up Asia's second-largest monolithic rock dome, engineered with multi-gate stone ramparts and granaries.
culturalSignificance: Dramatic fusion of Deccan hill-fort masonry, water cistern engineering, and nearby Hoysala temples at Aralaguppe.
description: Plains and hill-fort district crowned by Madhugiri monolith, Devarayanadurga, and 9th-century Nolamba temples; full records are under review.
history: Originally fortified by Raja Hira Gowda of the Madhugiri chieftains and later strengthened by Hyder Ali.

name: Udupi
monumentDescription: 13th-century coastal monastery complex founded by Madhvacharya featuring tiled coastal roofs, the Madhwa Sarovara tank, and Kanakana Kindi.
culturalSignificance: Center of Dvaita philosophy, the biennial Paryaya festival, Badaguthittu Yakshagana theatre, and Udupi's temple culinary lineage.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Tourism (KSTDC) & Sangeet Natak Akademi
description: Coastal cultural and culinary hub celebrated for Badaguthittu Yakshagana theatre, Sri Krishna Matha heritage, and vegetarian Udupi culinary traditions.
history: Evolved as a prominent center of Dvaita philosophy, classical Yakshagana prasanga traditions, and coastal temple cuisine.

name: Uttara Kannada
monumentDescription: Coastal sanctuary perched on Kanduka headland surrounded on three sides by the Arabian Sea, crowned by its monumental 20-storey Raja Gopura.
culturalSignificance: Anchors Uttara Kannada's coastal-ghat heritage alongside Kadamba-era Banavasi, Mirjan Fort, and Devarakadu sacred groves.
description: Coastal and Sahyadri forest district linking Kanduka coastal shrines, Mirjan Fort, and Kadamba-capital Banavasi; full archival monographs pending.
history: Banavasi in Uttara Kannada served as the first native royal capital of Karnataka under the Kadamba dynasty in the 4th century CE.

name: Vijayanagara
geoBoundaryNote: Carved out of Ballari on November 17, 2021; represented within the Ballari boundary polygon in the 2021 geoBoundaries LGD snapshot.
monumentDescription: 15th–16th century Vijayanagara granite masterpiece housing the iconic interlocking Stone Chariot and 56 musical monolithic pillars.
culturalSignificance: Heart of the UNESCO World Heritage Group of Monuments at Hampi (Ref. 241, 1986), exemplifying medieval Deccan urbanism and stonecraft.
description: Karnataka's 31st district, encompassing the UNESCO World Heritage Group of Monuments at Hampi along the Tungabhadra River.
history: Hampi served as the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire (14th–16th centuries CE) and was inscribed by UNESCO in 1986 under Reference No. 241.
heritageSites: Group of Monuments at Hampi (UNESCO Ref. 241, 1986)

name: Vijayapura
monumentDescription: 17th-century Adil Shahi mausoleum completed in 1656 CE, crowned by one of the world's largest unsupported masonry domes and an acoustic Whispering Gallery.
culturalSignificance: Pinnacle of Deccan Indo-Islamic structural engineering alongside Ibrahim Rauza, Bara Kaman, and Malik-e-Maidan.
description: Deccan architectural capital of the Adil Shahi dynasty, centered around Gol Gumbaz and Ibrahim Rauza; full festival and craft monographs pending.
history: Built as the capital of the Bijapur Sultanate (1490–1686 CE), yielding landmark pendentive domes and basalt civic waterworks.

name: Yadgir
monumentDescription: Hilltop fortress perched on a dramatic granite monolith overlooking the Bhima valley, preserving Adil Shahi and Vijayanagara masonry, bastions, and rock tanks.
culturalSignificance: Marks the Bhima–Krishna riverine corridor connecting Yadgir Fort, Shahpur Sleeping Buddha hills, and Shorapur heritage.
monumentAttribution: Karnataka State Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage
description: Bhima river basin district formed in 2010, home to Yadgir Fort and Surpur historical heritage; full cultural archives are in preparation.
history: Shaped by Yadava, Bahmani, Adil Shahi, and Surpur Bedar Nayaka administrations.
